candidates.label: Straight Street, Old City of Damascus
candidates.support: A colonnaded street running east-west through the Old City of Damascus, on the line of the city's main Roman-era street, is traditionally identified with the street called Straight in Acts. Part of it is still known locally as Derb el-Mustakim ("Straight Street"), though it is uncertain whether the name has been used continuously since antiquity; today the street is called Souk Medhat Pasha along part of its course.

summary.text: The street called Straight is the Damascus street where, according to Acts, the disciple Ananias found Saul of Tarsus (later the apostle Paul) praying after his encounter on the road to Damascus, and there restored his sight. A colonnaded street on this line still crosses the Old City of Damascus today, part of it still locally called by a name meaning "Straight Street," though it is uncertain whether that name has been used without a break since the first century.

history.text: Acts describes a vision in which the Lord told Ananias to go to "the street which is called Straight" and ask at the house of Judas for Saul of Tarsus, who was praying there after being blinded on the road to Damascus; Ananias obeyed, and Saul's sight was restored.

The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia notes that the old city of Damascus still follows its Roman-era street plan, and that part of its ancient colonnaded east-west street is still known as Derb el-Mustakim, "the straight street," though the encyclopedia does not claim this name has been used without interruption since antiquity.

politicalHistory.entity: Roman province of Syria (ruler: Imperial legates, governed from Antioch)
politicalHistory.note: Administers the Cilician plain throughout, and administered Philip's former tetrarchy directly for a few years after his death (34-37; Antiquities 18.4.6).
